key_insight: Solaris extends action-conditioned video world models to the multiplayer domain by learning to simulate consistent, multi-view observations from multi-agent gameplay, enabled by a purpose-built multiplayer data collection system.
problem_solved: Existing video world models are confined to single-agent perspectives and cannot capture multi-agent interactions or maintain coherence across multiple simultaneous views.
method: Design a multiplayer data system for robust, continuous, and automated collection of synchronized multi-agent, multi-view video streams in Minecraft.
Train an action-conditioned video world model on the collected multiplayer data so it can predict future observations for multiple players/ cameras simultaneously.
Enforce cross-view synchronization and consistency during modeling to ensure coherent multi-view simulation of interactions.
impact: Solaris enables realistic, multi-agent video world modeling that supports research on multi-agent planning, emergent interactions, and simulation-driven training for game AI and embodied agents, improving realism and generalization over single-agent models.

paper_title: Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft
paper_authors: Georgy Savva, Oscar Michel, Daohan Lu, Suppakit Waiwitlikhit, Timothy Meehan
